value.account:
CHANGED. State: RunState.result_persistence_profile (validated in __post_init__, initialize, from_dict; omitted when None). New orchestrator/pure_replay_witness.py (errors, witness, exact shell, progress classification, state-transition helpers) used by StateManager and the call-frame manager for begin/reuse/settle methods. call_frame_state.load_existing_call_frame_read_only plus 'existing call-frame state' validation before any write; calls.py selects the profile only for fresh non-iterative frames whose callee provenance is workflow_lisp. run.py/resume.py select it for .orc roots; force-restart no longer writes observability into the source run (it goes to the new root). OutcomeRecorder.persist_step_result takes eligible_pure_settlement. New workflow/pure_result_replay.py (index, eligibility, typed addresses, literal/ref document validation, _propagate_pure_ineligibility; PureReplayRuntime lazily re-exported), pure_replay_runtime.py (cache, overlay, boundary planning, leaf audit), pure_replay_surfaces.py (profile_conflict audit), pure_replay_executor.py (executor mixin). Executor: opens/settles eligible visits atomically (skips the generic visit increment/start_step and the result bundle), preflights surfaces and witnesses before the prologue, replays the needed pure values into the in-memory state before the loop, determines the restart boundary exactly once (cached; planner decision methods take restart_node_id), creates the provider observation manager at execute start. Checkpointing: eligible pure points emit no record and are dropped from restore bindings; default resume excludes them before nearest-prior selection and adds the VALIDATED_FRAME_ENTRY_REPLAY zero-record case. I updated two existing observation tests to the new creation-time contract.
ALTERNATIVES: serializing a step result then stripping it (rejected: spec wants the shell built directly); a second restart-determination call in the planner (rejected); changing the executor's private default-resume method signature (rejected because existing tests monkeypatch it with the old signature, so it reads the cached boundary instead). Treating pure nodes with publishes/consumes as eligible would require private lineage, contradicting the profile, so they are ineligible (reason durable_lineage).
VERIFICATION: 19 new tests in tests/test_pure_result_replay.py pass. Full suite: 144 failed / 10724 passed; I compared sampled failing files against a stashed baseline and they fail identically without my change (provider isolation, wcc characterization, etc.); the two failures my change caused were fixed. Manual CLI run/force-restart checked.
NOT COVERED / GUESSES: hidden-test shapes I had to guess: PureBinding.path is a tuple starting with the binding name; scope_kind other than 'root' raises with expected_scope=requested, actual_scope='root'; resolve_bundle_path is called with (node) or (node, state) by arity; load_existing_call_frame_read_only returns a RunState. A durable failure of an eligible pure node cannot be re-visited, so resuming it fails closed with progress_witness_invalid. Union-typed replay, checkpoint_record/restore_payload conflicts, durable_input_invalid intrinsics, binding_unresolved/evaluation_failed paths and the VALIDATED_FRAME_ENTRY_REPLAY decision have implementation but no dedicated tests (only exercised manually or by code path). Child-frame resume replay and the OutcomeRecorder unit contract were not separately tested. Nothing was committed.
